newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on firm cash, demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on firm cash, demand.

text.p: Firm nearby cash basis markets, light farmer selling plus active domestic and export demand buoyed CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.

"People thought the market yesterday (Thursday) was over-influenced by wheat plus the basis continues to appreciate. Also a hard look at usage numbers tells us it was overdone yesterday," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

Soybeans dropped in late trading Thursday as the wheat market plummeted to new contract lows. But wheat held firm during Friday's session and rallied into the close on signals that market also was oversold during Thursday's skid.
Nearby November soybeans closed at an 1-1/2 cents per bushel inverse with the January, further evidence of a strong demand-led market, the traders said.
USDA's export sales report Thursday, which showed U.S. soybean sales during the week ended October 17 at nearly 1.4 million tonnes, continued to capture attention as a key bullish fundamental.
There were differences of opinion, but in general the market was looking for no more than 1.0 million tonnes.
Soybeans closed 2-1/2 to 4-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with November up four at $7.00-1/2.

Support also came from news that Brazil may have bought 300,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans, signals that China continues to buy soybeans and soy products and on slow U.S. farmer selling of his newly-harvested beans, traders said.

On the domestic front, cash indicators remained supportive with the National Oilseed Processors Association weekly soybean crush at 28,632,000 bushels for the week ended October 23, up from 27,886,000 the previous week and above the 28,021,000 bushels crushed during the corresponding week a year ago.
But gains were curbed by forecasts for better-than-expected harvest weather over the weekend in the U.S. Midwest.

Technical indicators showed November moving closer to neutral territory on a short term basis with the nine day relative strength index (RSI) closing at 39 points. An RSI of 30 or less is generally considered an oversold market and 70 or more is near overbought status.
But the key moving averages for November continued to emit bearish signals.
The session high for November was $7.04 and low at $6.92. First support for November was at $6.92 and first resistance was at $7.04.

Prudential Securities bought two million bushels each of November and January, ADM Investor Services bought 1.5 million November and Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, sold two million bu of November, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CME at 68,000, down from 80,952 Thursday.

In soybean options, Cargill Investor Services sold 300 March $7.50 calls at nine cents, Lind Waldock bought 250 January $6.75 puts at nine cents and Tenco Inc sold 200 January $7.25 calls at 7-1/2 to eight cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 20,000, down from 22,558 Thursday.
